cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven strip-cloth boubou/tobe with embroidered pocket motifs, a garment style characteristic of West African Muslim men's dress (Wolof, Hausa, Mande, etc.); it fits the claimed Wolof attribution as a plausible regional garment.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou tilbi) composed of 153 narrow strips about 3 ¼ inches wide, hand-woven from (apparently) imported European white cotton thread, and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The body of the cloth has been assembled vertically, while the sleeves are assembled horizontally. The front of the gown has a large pocket sewn on. Both the pocket and the surrounding areas are embroidered using a shiny European off-white thread (probably rayon) with a series of concentric circles with much use of buttonhole eyelet stitching. Next to the pocket is a spiral and a decorative circle, the shoulders are decorated with panels, whilst the back has a large panel with concentric circles and spirals. The gown is hemmed and unlined.
